run_overlap.hash: polynomial mod 2^64, base 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15|1, H(i) = sum_k b[i+k] * base^k
run_overlap.rule: a candidate chunk is dropped if run_windows consecutive window-byte windows aligned to its own grid, none constant (all bytes equal), each occur at ANY offset of ANY 0018 pinned blob; run_windows x window = 1024 shared bytes

rule.note: the three pinned archives carry .exe members only (Go's toolchain binaries, node.exe, PuTTY's programs); no .dll matches

sources.why_these: the same five real families as 0018, from DIFFERENT projects: no file here is another edition of a 0018 pinned project (CPython, SQLite), no pinned RFC number is repeated, and no RFC that obsoletes, updates, is obsoleted by or is updated by a 0018-pinned RFC is drawn (the RFC Editor's index annotations, both directions). corpus.what: a second real-content fit corpus from NEW pinned upstream files of 0018's five real families, built pre-freeze by tools/pivot/corpus_realfit2.py and sealed by array hash; nothing under data/pivot is committed
corpus.why_three_doublings: Rung 4 + d holds 0021's whole block plus, per family, the first n_f x (2^d - 1) chunks with rows of 0024's seeded pool, n_f being the family's chunks with rows in 0021's block: every rung therefore holds exactly 2^d times rung 4's plaintexts of every family, the family mix of 0021's block is preserved to the chunk (py_src carries r1 0.6486, r2 0.6538, r3 0.6543, r4 0.6527, r5 0.6527, r6 0.6525, r7 0.6528 of the rows), a lower rung is a subset of the next, and the abscissa is exact. The pool order is the nesting order, so the rungs are one corpus growing rather than three draws. The rows of a new rung are permuted whole by a sealed stream so that M4's last-10 percent validation split is a random tenth of the rung; rungs 1..4 keep 0023's order (the reproduction). Three doublings, not more, because py_src - 0.6527 of 0021's rows - needed 4704 new plaintexts with rows and the fourteen pinned Python projects yield 5781 candidate chunks; a fourth doubling would need 10080.

cost.estimate_stated_in_advance: a range, from banked numbers. Linear in rows from 0023's rung-4 seconds: model about r1 45 s, r2 90 s, r3 178 s, r4 356 s, r5 712 s, r6 1420 s, r7 2844 s; logistic about r1 8 s, r2 16 s, r3 33 s, r4 66 s, r5 131 s, r6 262 s, r7 524 s; trees seconds; the null on the top rung about 927 s; the shift arm about rung 4's; in all about 8097 s of fits (2.2 hours). The cap-bound: 0023 banked 5.734 s per iteration for the model and 0.167 s for the logistic at rung 4 (62 and 392 iterations), and the model's iteration count grew with rows over the first decade ([31, 36, 47, 62]); if the new rungs run to the sealed caps (250 and 1000) with per-iteration time scaling with rows, the new rungs cost r5 2871 s, r6 5725 s, r7 11467 s for the model and r5 334 s, r6 667 s, r7 1336 s for the logistic, 24604 s in all (6.8 hours). Between 2.2 and 6.8 hours of fits on this machine at three threads, plus the scoring-set materialisation, the row-identity scan over both fit corpora and twenty-five scorings; the top rung's model fit is one uncheckpointable stretch of up to that size. COULD NOT VERIFY until run - the banked seconds are the measurement.

design_decisions.expected_outcome: On the curve: SECOND_DECADE_RISES, more likely than not, but less likely than 0023's pass was. For: 0023's second half rose at 0.007344 per doubling with an interval [0.006199, 0.00846] well clear of the bar, and the new content is the same five kinds. Against: 0023's rise was measured on the scored files' own unscored chunks; every reading the record has of content the model did not see is flat (0018/0019, 0015), and the new files are other projects - the per-plaintext rate on other files could be anywhere between 0023's and 0. On the lead: LINEAR_LEADS or NO_SEPARATION, more likely than MODEL_LEADS. For: over the first decade the logistic bought 0.002207 more per doubling than the model with a paired interval entirely below 0, the model's lead shrank to 0.0014 at rung 4, and the straight lines cross before the first new doubling (arithmetic sealed under reference_slopes_informational). Against: the model's rung-to-rung gains fell over the first decade while the logistic's did not, which could as easily reverse on new files; and the paired interval of a difference of about 0.005 over 38452 rows in 1500 chunks may include 0. Either outcome on either question is published at the same size in the same places; the verdict string names both.
design_decisions.first_decade_reproduced_not_reused: rungs 1..4 are refitted (0023's rungs row for row) rather than copied from 0023's artifact: a machinery that no longer reproduces the first decade is not allowed to measure the second, and the twelve readings must land within 0.005 of 0023's banked values (the runner files NOT RUN on the first drift it sees, at rung 4, before any new plaintext is fitted)
design_decisions.no_replicate: a second nesting of the new rungs would double the pool and the fits; 0023's replicate read the fit-side variance at the smallest rung once; the sealed file names the second seed as what this does not cover
design_decisions.null_on_the_top_rung: the null control permutes the TOP rung's labels (in rung order) with np.random.default_rng([seed2, 200]) and fits M4 on that rung; the permuted array is computed here from the sealed corpora and its hash sealed; it is the first role in the order so that no other draw precedes it and so that the largest block is probed first
design_decisions.recipes_are_fixed: 0021's M4, L3 and D1 verbatim, as 0023 sealed them; no search
design_decisions.reproduction_before_any_new_plaintext: null on the top rung; rung 4 (0021's block: the reproduction of 0021 and of 0023's top rung); rungs 1, 2, 3 (the reproduction of 0023's curve) - every reproduction before any new plaintext is fitted; rungs 5, 6, 7 ascending; then the shift arm; the model last within each rung
design_decisions.rungs_nested_on_0021s_block_in_exact_dou: Rung 4 + d holds 0021's whole block plus, per family, the first n_f x (2^d - 1) chunks with rows of 0024's seeded pool, n_f being the family's chunks with rows in 0021's block: every rung therefore holds exactly 2^d times rung 4's plaintexts of every family, the family mix of 0021's block is preserved to the chunk (py_src carries r1 0.6486, r2 0.6538, r3 0.6543, r4 0.6527, r5 0.6527, r6 0.6525, r7 0.6528 of the rows), a lower rung is a subset of the next, and the abscissa is exact. The pool order is the nesting order, so the rungs are one corpus growing rather than three draws. The rows of a new rung are permuted whole by a sealed stream so that M4's last-10 percent validation split is a random tenth of the rung; rungs 1..4 keep 0023's order (the reproduction). Three doublings, not more, because py_src - 0.6527 of 0021's rows - needed 4704 new plaintexts with rows and the fourteen pinned Python projects yield 5781 candidate chunks; a fourth doubling would need 10080.

seed2_and_its_stream_words.why_distinct: SeedSequence pads short entropy with zeros, so [seed2, 0] would be seed2's own stream; every use of seed2 here carries a distinct second word

design_decisions.the_0021_bar_flag_uses_the_tree_alone: 0021's clause (best trivial baseline on the same rows plus 0.05) re-applied at the top rung, banked twice and labelled: against the depth-3 tree plus 0.05 (the tree stood in for the best of 0021's four baselines; the other three read below it at 0021 and are not refitted here, so that flag can only be optimistic), and against the higher of the tree and the standardised logistic plus 0.05 (OPERATING_RULES 4a names logistic regression among the trivial baselines; 0021's four did not include it, and L3 is fitted at every rung here). Neither is a verdict.
design_decisions.the_bootstrap_clause: the 2.5th percentile of the model's second-decade slope under the sealed cluster bootstrap over the scored real chunks is > 0. The interval is over the scored chunks only and does not resample the fit side; a slope at or above the bar whose interval reaches 0 is SECOND_DECADE_FLAT: four points and a rise the scored chunks do not agree on is not a rise.
design_decisions.the_clause_is_the_second_decade: the model's SECOND-decade slope, in real-family accuracy per doubling of plaintexts over rungs 4..7, >= 0.005. The bar is 0023's restated, a design choice made before any second-decade number exists: the rise the record agreed in 0016 and 0023 to call a rise, about two thirds of 0023's measured 0.007344 and about half the builder's per-plaintext rate. It is not the instrument's resolution: 0023's scored-chunk intervals were about 0.0011 per doubling wide either side. 'The record's rate' in this document always means 0.005 per doubling; the second-minus-first-decade slope is quoted in the same sentence as any pass. 0.005 over 3.0 doublings is an end-to-end rise of 0.015, 577 rows of 38452. A pass is 'keeps rising at the bar on other files of the same kinds', not 'rises like the first decade'.
design_decisions.the_lead_rule_is_in_the_verdict_string: the 95 percent paired cluster-bootstrap interval of model minus logistic real-family top-1 at the top rung, over the scored real chunks with the slope bootstrap's own resamples: entirely above 0 is MODEL_LEADS, entirely below 0 is LINEAR_LEADS, otherwise NO_SEPARATION (never 'equal'); the verdict string carries it as a suffix. If the model or the logistic at the top rung is at its iteration cap, the suffix is still read by the rule, but every document that states it states '(the <role> at its iteration cap at the top rung)' in the same sentence and the lead is not quoted as a recipe comparison, exactly as the difference flag is not. This is not a pass/fail clause: each of the three readings is a legitimate outcome and the verdict string carries whichever the interval gives, beside the curve part. No document quotes the curve part without the lead part.
design_decisions.the_second_decade_reading: the reader names what the second-decade slope did beside any FLAT: a slope whose scored-chunk interval sits entirely below 0 is published as 'adding files of the same kinds lowered the model's reading on the original files', beside the per-family second-decade slopes and the shift arm; a slope between 0 and the bar as 'below the record's rate; whether it is flat is not resolved here'.
design_decisions.the_shift_arm: rung 5's new plaintexts alone - per family the first n_f chunks with rows of 0024's pool, none of 0021's block - with rows permuted by np.random.default_rng([20260917, 150]); informational: read beside rung 4 (the same plaintext count, the scored files' own chunks) as a direct reading of what other files of the same families buy for the original files. 1029 plaintexts, 26420 rows: exactly rung 5's new chunks, so no extra plaintext is drawn for it. Its readings, its difference from rung 4 (what other files buy for the original files at the same plaintext count) and its difference from rung 5 (what the original files' own chunks add on top of it) are banked as flags.
design_decisions.the_two_0021_bar_flags: 0021's clause (best trivial baseline on the same rows plus 0.05) re-applied at the top rung, banked twice and labelled: against the depth-3 tree plus 0.05 (the tree stood in for the best of 0021's four baselines; the other three read below it at 0021 and are not refitted here, so that flag can only be optimistic), and against the higher of the tree and the standardised logistic plus 0.05 (OPERATING_RULES 4a names logistic regression among the trivial baselines; 0021's four did not include it, and L3 is fitted at every rung here). Neither is a verdict.
design_decisions.why_the_lead_is_named_in_the_verdict: 0023's open question was whether the linear rule overtakes the model; a flag can be left unquoted, a verdict suffix cannot, so the verdict string carries MODEL_LEADS, LINEAR_LEADS or NO_SEPARATION beside RISES or FLAT and no document quotes one part without the other

what_it_found.expected_outcome_vs_measured: the sealed file expected SECOND_DECADE_RISES more likely than not (less likely than 0023's pass), and LINEAR_LEADS or NO_SEPARATION more likely than MODEL_LEADS; the run read SECOND_DECADE_RISES_MODEL_LEADS.
what_it_found.one_line: The second decade of real plaintexts rises — and the boosted model still leads the hand-writable linear rule at the top rung: the model's second-decade slope is 0.00697 per doubling (interval [0.00571, 0.00824]) against 0.005; at the top rung model minus logistic is 0.0039 (paired interval [0.0001, 0.0077]), MODEL_LEADS by the sealed rule.
what_it_found.the_curve: the model reads [0.0974, 0.1065, 0.1139, 0.1193, 0.1236, 0.13, 0.1404] over [130, 258, 515, 1029, 2058, 4116, 8232] plaintexts; second-decade slopes model 0.00697 ([0.00571, 0.00824]), logistic 0.00638 ([0.0052, 0.00756]), tree -0.0003 ([-0.00073, 0.00012]); both clauses pass: the model's second-decade slope is at or above 0.005 and the interval's lower bound above 0.0 — `SECOND_DECADE_RISES`. The logistic's second-decade slope (0.00638) clears the same bar and the tree's (-0.0003) does not: a rise the linear rule shares is a rise of the cheap signal, not of the recipe.
what_it_found.the_lead: the model leads the standardised logistic by 0.0039 (paired interval [0.0001, 0.0077], entirely above 0); at rung 4 the same reading is 0.0014 ([-0.002303, 0.0047], NO_SEPARATION); model minus logistic by rung [0.0063, 0.0126, 0.0054, 0.0014, -0.0005, -0.0021, 0.0039]; over the second decade the slope difference is 0.00059 ([-0.00102, 0.00231]): the paired interval includes 0: not resolved at this size; never read as 'equal'.
what_it_found.the_shift_arm: The shift arm — rung 5's new plaintexts alone (1029 plaintexts, 26420 rows: rung 4's count, none of 0021's block) — reads model 0.1184, logistic 0.118, tree 0.0923: against rung 4 by -0.0009, 0.0001 and -0.0006, against rung 5 by -0.0052, -0.0061 and 0.0002 — the direct reading of what other files of the same families buy for the original files at the same count, informational.
what_it_found.what_it_means_for_the_record: other files of the same kinds keep buying the recipe the record's rate on the files it is scored on, through 8232 plaintexts (eight times 0021's), so the budget excuse is answered a second time on real content, this time with other files; at eight times 0021's plaintexts the boosted recipe still leads a rule a person can write out on the record's own real content, by 0.0039 — the recipe conclusion of 0021, 0022 and 0023 (that the linear rule gets most of the signal) is bounded by the size of that lead, not reversed. Not a transfer reading, and not 0023's in-distribution reading either: every rung holds the scored files' own unscored chunks, and the plaintexts added above rung 4 are other files of the same kinds, so the second decade confounds more plaintexts with plaintexts from other files, which the shift arm reads directly. No extrapolation beyond the top rung is banked or quoted. Nothing here revises 0003, 0014, 0015, 0016, 0017, 0018, 0019, 0021, 0022 or 0023, and nothing here establishes a buyer.

why_this_exists: 0023 read REAL_CURVE_RISES: over 130 to 1029 real plaintexts the model rose 0.007344 per doubling (interval [0.006199, 0.00846]), the standardised logistic 0.009551 ([0.008478, 0.010649]) and the depth-3 tree 0.003002; model minus logistic -0.002207 with a paired interval [-0.003707, -0.000752] entirely below 0, and the model's lead over the logistic by rung was [0.0063, 0.0126, 0.0054, 0.0014], 0.0014 at the top. The top rung was 0021's whole fit block - every chunk of the five pinned files that the sealed evaluation set does not use - so the record held no more real plaintexts, and 0023 named 'a second decade' and 'more real content than 0021's fit block (no such corpus exists in the record)' as what it did not cover. Two questions follow directly from its numbers.
